# QuarterSmart

> QuarterSmart is an early-adoption AI partner for owner-led businesses, based in Mesa, Arizona. We track new AI launches, early-access programs, quiet product updates and credible reports, tell each business which ones matter to it, then set the tools up in its own accounts and train the team to use them. Promise: know what changed in AI the day it lands, and have it working in your business while it is still early. Short form: AI early adoption, setup and training.

QuarterSmart works with owner-led and operator-led businesses of roughly 10 to 250 people across the United States. Our approach has two halves, summed up as "Train your team. Automate the rest." First we train the team on a new tool inside their own work, then we automate the repetitive work that is left, with agents and workflows the team can see and check.

"Day one" always means the first day a tool is available to your account. Rollouts are often staggered by plan, region or company size, so we prepare before that day and start setup as soon as access arrives. We cannot promise early access; vendors control it. We tell clients when a waitlist or beta opens and help them apply.

QuarterSmart is independent and is not affiliated with or endorsed by OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Microsoft or any other AI vendor. Product names are trademarks of their owners.

## Founder
Hyrum Hurst founded QuarterSmart and is the person clients work with directly: he writes every Signal and sets up the assistants, agents and automations himself. There are no account managers or hand-offs.

Hyrum Hurst is also CTO of Learning Journey AI (https://learningjourneyai.com/), an AI education company in Washington, DC, where he runs the platform, the website and the course-creation workflows. Staying current on applied AI is part of that job, and QuarterSmart puts the same habit to work for its clients.

- Job titles: Founder, QuarterSmart. CTO, Learning Journey AI.
- Works in: Claude, ChatGPT and n8n, every day, on live client work.
- Other roles: AI automation consultant (contract) for Dual Logic, a Washington, DC AI integration consultancy; pro bono AI work for Ability Builders, a Mesa nonprofit. These are his own roles, not QuarterSmart clients.
- Verified n8n creator. Quoted in CyberNews on local AI models. Registered expert source on Qwoted.
- Profile page: https://quartersmart.com/about/hyrum-hurst

## Signals
Signals is QuarterSmart's free, public coverage of AI launches, published at https://quartersmart.com/signals with a Monday email, Signals Weekly. Each Signal says what happened, whether it matters and to whom, and ends in a verdict: Act now, Prepare, Wait or Ignore. Wait and Ignore are common verdicts.

Every Signal carries one status label:
- Reported: publicly reported, not confirmed by the company. Always shown as "Reported · unconfirmed."
- Confirmed: announced by the company, not yet available to most accounts.
- Available: usable now, on the plans listed.
- Early access: a waitlist, beta or preview is open.
- Quiet update: a change inside a tool you may already pay for.
- Event: a launch event we are covering.

Sourcing: public information only. No confidential documents, credentials, private source code or anything obtained by breaking terms of service. Reported items stay labeled unconfirmed until the company confirms or denies them. Sources are cited, other people's screenshots are linked rather than re-hosted, and corrections are logged with timestamps. The accuracy record for reported items, including misses, is the Signals Log. Signals is general information about third-party products, not legal, security or financial advice.

## Ways to work with us
The services ladder, from free to ongoing:
1. Signals (free): the public feed and the Signals Weekly email.
2. Head Start (from $1,500, one time): a review of the software a business already pays for, looking for AI features it has not switched on, with the three most relevant launches or tools, each with a verdict, and a 30-day plan. About a week from kickoff. The full fee counts toward a Day One Setup or the first month of First Quarter if the client starts within 30 days.
3. Day One Setup (from $2,500 per tool): one tool set up properly in the client's accounts with least-access permissions, connected to email, calendar, docs or CRM, tested with a few people first, then taught to the team.
4. Rollout Session (quoted): live, role-based team training on a tool the team already has, using the team's own work.
5. First Quarter membership (from $1,500 a month; Pro from $3,500 a month): Client Signals filtered to the member's own tools and delivered the same business day for anything that affects their stack, setup and training time every month, and priority on launch weeks.
6. Build (scoped): custom agents and automations for work that repeats, scoped after a Head Start or for members.

Agencies and IT providers can resell Signals and Day One Setups through the Partner Bench (see For Agencies).
